#1700. Thomas Tuchel responds to Morgan Rogers' Cole Palmer defence

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 19:44

England manager Thomas Tuchel has responded to Morgan Rogers' passionate defence of Cole Palmer after the Chelsea midfielder branded suggestions that his teammate lacks commitment to the national team "a lie".

Rogers spoke out following England's 2-1 Nations League victory over Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, a result that secured the Three Lions' place in the quarter-finals of the competition.

The 24-year-old, who opened the scoring against Croatia, dismissed claims that Palmer does not want to represent his country, insisting that the Chelsea playmaker's recent international absences have been related to managing his fitness.

Palmer was omitted from Tuchel's latest squad despite featuring regularly for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso this season, having previously withdrawn from international duty because of injury concerns.

The England manager had suggested that Palmer was missing too many opportunities to impress, prompting further questions about the 24-year-old's standing within the national team.

However, when Rogers' comments were put to Tuchel after the Croatia victory, the German appeared unconcerned by his player's public intervention.

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Tuchel made it clear that he had no issue with Rogers defending his Chelsea teammate and long-time friend.

"It's totally fine. He's his team-mate and I guess his friend, so why wouldn't he?" Tuchel told reporters.

The England boss explained that he had not heard the full interview and therefore did not wish to comment directly on its contents.

Instead, he praised Rogers' contribution against Croatia, highlighting the commitment he had demonstrated throughout the encounter.

"I think he was the standout player today, offensively and defensively, and that's what matters," Tuchel added.

Rogers had earlier delivered an emphatic response when asked about the suggestion that Palmer was reluctant to play for England.

"It's a lie. He wants to be here," Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live, before explaining that the midfielder had been eager to receive another international call-up.

The two players have known each other since their time in Manchester City's academy and are now teammates at both Chelsea and international level.

Rogers revealed that Palmer had endured a particularly difficult period with injuries last season and had struggled to feel fully comfortable on the pitch.

The former Aston Villa attacker argued that carefully managing those physical problems was necessary to protect Palmer's long-term career.

He also expressed frustration that the player's absence had been interpreted as evidence of insufficient dedication to England, rather than a decision influenced by his fitness.

Rogers hopes Palmer will return to international duty in the near future, believing his quality would be a significant asset to Tuchel's squad.

Despite Rogers' intervention, Palmer still faces a difficult challenge in establishing himself as a regular member of Tuchel's England squad.

The Chelsea attacker was overlooked for the 2026 World Cup following an injury-disrupted campaign and has made only three appearances for England since Tuchel took charge in January 2025.

His absence from the November squad was particularly notable because he has returned to regular club football, recording five goals and three assists in his opening 11 appearances of the 2026-27 season.

When explaining his decision to leave Palmer out of the squad earlier this month, Tuchel acknowledged the midfielder's desire to represent England but stressed the importance of being available during international camps.

The German also pointed to the strength of his attacking options, with Jude Bellingham, Eberechi Eze, Rogers and Fulham youngster Josh King all competing for opportunities in advanced positions.

Palmer's situation has already attracted support from Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, who previously defended the decision to withdraw from international duty when the midfielder was experiencing physical discomfort.

Tuchel has insisted that the door remains open for Palmer, although his selection decisions suggest that availability and involvement in training camps will remain important considerations.

England will complete their Nations League group campaign against Spain in Madrid on Sunday, November 15, having already secured qualification for the quarter-finals.

Palmer will again be absent, leaving Tuchel with another opportunity to assess the attacking players currently ahead of him in the international pecking order.

Rogers, meanwhile, strengthened his own case for further involvement with his performance against Croatia, earning particular praise from the manager whose selection policy he was indirectly questioning.

#1699. De Rossi admits Genoa ‘lost well’ to Milan and recalls Moreira’s comment: “Even our opponents notice”

Daniele De Rossi has looked back at Genoa’s defeat to AC Milan and how he wasn’t frustrated with his team afterwards.

Milan entered the international break with a much-needed victory against Genoa, but it wasn’t the easiest result of the season. After a disappointing defeat to Ferencvaros – which extended the midweek run of defeats – they couldn’t afford to drop points, and they succeeded, even if it wasn’t without flaw.

With two goals inside 20 minutes, you’d be forgiven for expecting Milan to win by more than a couple. However, that was the end of their goalscoring for the afternoon and although Genoa pulled one back, they didn’t grab more than a consolation goal.

Speaking to Sky Sport – in the new series ‘Radici’ – De Rossi looked back on the defeat to the Rossoneri, as well as a comment that stuck with him from Diego Moreira, as MilanPress have relayed today.

We indeed lost against Milan, but we lost ‘well.’ We didn’t deserve it. Three or four weeks ago, the latest results seemed like a pipe dream. I thank the players, staff, and my club for giving me faith and patience at a time when other clubs wouldn’t have had it.

“They remembered how good we did last year. I’m happy to have emerged from a difficult period and to be Genoa’s coach; I’m really happy there.”

“I’m passionate about the fans and the supporters. I’m part of a club that, in terms of fan base, is among the best in Europe. I’m passionate; I don’t punch a clock. I spend two hours with the stockman or the waitress with the same enthusiasm I spend time with the team captain. Experiencing it like that, you realise that Genoa is a great team.

“Genoa is full of Genoese fans who remind you every second how much they love their club, the pride of being the top club in Italy. The architecture of the stadium and the warmth of the fans… I’m not saying this to be a sycophant, but on Sunday Moreira came to me and said, ‘I’ve never seen anything like this here in Italy.’ It’s a reality that even our opponents notice.”

#1698. Building in Barca and the Jim Reaper strikes again

Greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

Of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

Elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

Mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Meanwhile, the big news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

He was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

For further reading, check out my weekly column in which I look at three ways in which Arsenal have evolved this season.

#1697. An Arseblog update

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Big Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”

As of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a plan for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very big way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

So, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most important thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

Finland will conclude their Nations League C campaign on Sunday, when they welcome San Marino to Bolt Arena.

The hosts come into the final clash of the group stage in third place with seven points, while the visitors are last in fourth with no points, and neither can secure promotion.

Finland are certain of their place in Nations League C in the next iteration of the competition, but because second-placed Belarus have 10 points and boast a better head-to-head record, the highest they can finish is third.

The hosts' hopes of promotion ended when they lost 2-0 against Albania on November 12, which was their second consecutive defeat.

It was also the third time in four games that they failed to score, though they have only conceded four goals in the group stage so far.

Head coach Jacob Friis deserves credit for his team's resilience at home given they have won four, drawn one and lost just one of their last six outings as hosts.

Finland kept two clean sheets in those six home clashes, while they did not concede more than one goal in any of those matches.

San Marino would have been relegated in previous editions of the Nations League, but Nations League D will not exist from 2028-29, meaning they cannot be demoted.

It would be wrong to suggest the visitors have improved in any meaningful way, but after conceding 10 goals in their opening three group matches, conceding four times in their next two clashes could be seen as a small step in the right direction.

Manager Roberto Cevoli was in the dugout when his team were beaten 7-0 by Finland on September 26, and another loss this weekend would be his country's eighth consecutive defeat against their hosts.

The visitors' have failed to win any of their last 20 fixtures in all competitions, with the nation only earning one draw in that period, and a defeat on Sunday would extend their losing streak to eight games.

San Marino have also lost each of their 10 most recent away trips, a stretch in which they scored just five goals.

Finland have two players suspended for Sunday's match, with centre-back Miro Tenho having been sent off against Albania, while midfielder Adam Markhiev has now accumulated too many yellow cards.

Robert Ivanov came on in defence late in the game against Albania, and he can be expected to partner Tony Miettinen on Sunday.

In the middle of the pitch, Anssi Suhonen may be selected to feature alongside Kaan Kairinen and Leo Walta.

San Marino will hope that central defenders Marco Pasolini and Dante Rossi can protect shot-stopper Edoardo Colombo.

Fausto Salicioni is yet to find the back of the net in seven appearances for the national team, but he could be given another chance to impress alongside Nicola Nanni.

Filippo Fabbri picked up his second yellow card of the tournament last time out and must now serve a one-game ban.

#1692. Scott McTominay reveals hospital dash and heart shock treatment days before Scotland's World Cup opener

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:25 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 11 November 2026

Scott McTominay has revealed he needed a procedure to reset the beat of his heart just two days before Scotland’s World Cup campaign kicked off back in June.

Heading into the opening game against Haiti in Boston, the explanation given from the Scottish Football Association was that McTominay had been carrying a sickness bug.

But, after the squad had flown from their training base in Charlotte, McTominay had actually been whisked away to hospital straight from the airport via a police escort.

The 29-year-old had shock treatment on his heart before then going on to play all three games as Steve Clarke’s side were knocked out at the group stage.

The Napoli midfielder subsequently underwent corrective surgery back at the start of the season and missed Scotland’s opening four fixtures in the Nations League.

Now back in the squad ahead of the upcoming double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland, McTominay has opened up for the first time on his health issues.

Scott McTominay had a heart procedure two days before playing against Haiti

Scott McTominay in action during Scotland's 1-0 World Cup win over Haiti

Asked about what happened, he replied: ‘The sickness bug? You’re not going to say I have something to do with my heart two days before the first game of the World Cup. It’s not an ideal scenario being in the hospital two days before — well, technically 36 hours before the first game of the World Cup.

‘But you have to take the cards you’re dealt on the chin. It’s part of the game. There’s nothing I could do about it and the shock went well, I was back in normal rhythm then 24 hours later you’re playing a World Cup game.

‘The World Cup, it was difficult for me, to be honest. I had to go and get the shock on my heart. That was two days before the Haiti game.

‘You prepare so well, I was in such good condition and something like that happens. You’re thinking: “How has this happened to me?” But then you have to get on with it. That’s the cards you are dealt in football.

‘Sometimes things don’t go your way and you have to continue to do your best. It’s nowhere near an excuse but it’s something you have to look back on and say: “Well, it’s part of the process”.

McTominay was given full reassurance from the doctors and medical staff that the procedure had gone well, insisting it was never in his thoughts to pull out of the squad.

Asked whether it was playing on his mind across the three games against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil, he said: ‘No. I put it to bed. I tried my best to put it to bed anyway. Whenever you go under anaesthetic and you have to get put to sleep, it decreases the athletic performance a little bit and sleep and stuff like that.

‘You have to get back round to doing it again. It was far from ideal but those are the cards that you’re dealt, there’s nothing you can do about it.’

Some fans had questioned McTominay’s form throughout the World Cup, oblivious to the fact that he was effectively playing through an ongoing heart issue.

Asked whether the criticism bothered him at the time, he continued: ‘It’s tough. It’s never easy, things like that, but you can’t use things like that as an excuse because that’s just not in my nature.

‘I take whole responsibility for a lot of the things that we didn’t create or didn’t score the goals in the World Cup.

‘I can put my face out there and say that that was nowhere near good enough. But that’s part of football. You have to get away and think about it and reflect and come back a better player.

‘I didn’t know that’s what people were saying. I probably had an idea.

‘I’ve been criticised a million times before in my career before but I don’t let it get under my skin or worry too much about it. You know yourself as a professional footballer if you’re not quite where you should be.

‘For me, I had half an idea but you just try to block it out because if you think about negative things you might speak it into existence.’

Both teams are bidding to secure first position in the section, which would mean automatic qualification to League A for the next Nations League.

This is a really difficult match to call, and we are finding it difficult to separate them given Bosnia-Herzegovina's unbeaten campaign to date. The two teams could be forced to accept a share of the spoils on Saturday.

Portugal will officially begin life after the legendary Cristiano Ronaldo with a clash against Denmark in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday night.

Jorge Jesus' side have already booked their spot in the quarter-finals of the competition, while Denmark are battling to claim the second qualification spot in the section.

Denmark are more than capable of making this a tricky match for Portugal, and we are backing the visitors to score, but Jesus' side should be able to extend their 100% record in this season's competition.

#1687. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1686. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta faces Liverpool, Chelsea, Man City battle for 'standout' £29m striker in 2027

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 01:13

Arsenal could be joined in the race for Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi by Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners may have entered the international break as leaders in the Premier League, but there are still some concerns in the fanbase.

Mikel Arteta's side have only scored 15 goals in 10 top-flight matches, and that has naturally led to calls for the club to strengthen in attack in the January transfer window.

The Londoners have been linked to Tresoldi, with the Club Brugge striker currently valued at just over £29m by Transfermarkt.

However, a new report from Het Laatste Nieuws claims that the striker is also wanted by Premier League sides such as Liverpool, Chelsea and Man City.

Tresoldi has enjoyed a strong start to 2026-27, scoring 13 goals in 15 games for Club Brugge, including five times in four Champions League games.

Arteta will be pleased that the 22-year-old scored against Aston Villa and Inter Milan this season as it would suggest that the striker could adapt to a team in a more competitive league.

The biggest reason for the Gunners' interest in the forward is undoubtedly the underperformance of Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres, both of whom have disappointed for some time.

Gyokeres has only been trusted to start once in the Premier League this season, and he has routinely struggled against teams in the top half of the table.

Havertz has found it difficult to stay consistently fit, and his performances have been frustratingly mixed since signing for the Gunners in 2023.

The Gunners will almost certainly not face any serious competition from Liverpool, who already have Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike as options up front.

Manchester City could have interest in Tresoldi as a backup to Erling Haaland, though it remains to be seen how keen any player would be about moving to the Etihad due to the threat of sanctions following news of the club being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

Chelsea are known to be active in the transfer market irrespective of the depth they have, and there is a clear spot for the Club Brugge striker at Stamford Bridge as the backup to Joao Pedro.

Whether Tresoldi would accept a role as a backup is unclear, but the Blues are in a serious battle for a Champions League spot, whereas Arsenal will almost certainly secure a return to the top level of European football.

#1685. Moretto provides update on Milan’s Endrick and Tresoldi pursuits: “Really likes him”

In January, AC Milan will make some big investments, if reports are to be believed. Currently, two names are leading the talk.

It could be a big month for Milan if things go their way in January. They hope to add a central defender to their squad – and have hoped to do so since before the end of the summer mercato – but the headline signing may be an attacking option, with quite a few names in the mix.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The favourites are clear, though: Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi.

Speaking on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Matteo Moretto provided an update on the Rossoneri’s pursuit for both forwards and whether either was progressing, as MilanNews relayed.

“Although Mourinho continues to say that Endrick will stay at Real Madrid, the truth is that the player has the ball right now. If the player decides to tell Real Madrid that he wants to try a new experience to grow and play, Real Madrid will not object. And I can tell you that these are precisely the indications.

“To date, there have been no official communications between the parties, but I can confirm that Endrick, as he also stated in a recent interview, is open to a new loan experience, Lyon-style, which could give him that extra focus and playing time, also with a view to the national team.

“A few days ago, I told you how Milan were really close to signing Tresoldi a few years ago, so much so that the player arrived, visited Milanello, and stayed at Casa Milan; the contracts were even ready.

“I want to clarify that, since he was a very young player at the time, it wasn’t a deal directly supervised by Paolo Maldini. There were other people managing the deal. Ricky Massara was also Milan’s transfer manager at the time, and there were others as well.

“The deal never actually got signed because Milan stalled, and the player returned to Germany, effectively signing a new contract with Hannover. Beyond that, there’s a lot of talk about Tresoldi now in terms of Milan’s present and future.

“I want to clarify a few points, however. I can confirm that it’s true that Cardinale really likes him, and Milan really likes him. The club is evaluating what steps to take to make this kind of move…”

It’s clear that the Diavolo are keen to add some attacking firepower to their ranks in January, understandably. However, it must be the right fit and there are certainly a few questions about Tresoldi now, with the price only rising.

#1684. Linda Noskova vs Elina Svitolina - WTA Finals prediction, form, head-to-head

By Joel Lefevre | 14 Nov 2026 01:44, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 19:28

In a rematch from this year’s Stuttgart Open quarter-finals, Linda Noskova and Elina Svitolina square off in the WTA Finals semis on Saturday.

Both ladies finished the group stage at 2-1, with the Czech losing her last match to Jessica Pegula 6-7 (2-7) 6-4 5-7, and Svitolina ousting Aryna Sabalenka on Friday 6-3 3-6 6-1.

The group phase did not end the way she had envisioned, but Linda Noskova will hope to shake off her surprise defeat from Thursday as she enters the knockout stage of this tournament for the first time.

After losing the opening set to Pegula, it appeared as though the tide was turning in the Czech’s favour, but the reigning Wimbledon champion failed to covert her match point, losing three straight games in the final set, which sent her to defeat.

She is the youngest player to reach the semi-finals of this tournament since Petra Kvitova in 2011, and Noskova will hope to follow in that same path as the former Czech player went on to win that edition of the WTA Finals in what was her debut.

If Noskova wants to advance, she must be cleaner on serve, registering 15 double faults versus Pegula, six more than she committed in her first two matches at this event.

In her three group contests, the 21-year-old converted 14 break-point opportunities overall while conceding eight.

She has hit a total of 20 aces at the tournament so far and won over 60% of her first serves in all three of her matches.

In a roller coaster three-set outing on Friday afternoon, Svitolina came out on top, winning six straight games in the end.

It was her first win against Sabalenka in six years as the Ukrainian earned a berth in the semis-finals of this event for the first time since 2019.

For a while it looked like Svitolina was going to throw it away, failing to convert four match points before finally claiming victory.

As a result, she has a chance to advance to the final of this tournament for a third time in her last three appearances.

Not since the 2017 WTA Finals group stage has she lost a match in this tournament when winning the opening set.

Svitolina has converted 11 break point opportunities in her last two outings after failing to convert six chances in her opener.

Third match: vs. Jessica Pegula 6-7 (7-2) 6-4 5-7

Second match: vs. Karolina Muchova 3-6 6-2 6-2

Third match: vs. Aryna Sabalenka 6-3 3-6 6-1

Australian Open (2024) - Round of 16: Noskova wins 3-0 walkover

Monterrey Open (2024) - Quarter-finals: Noskova wins 6-4 6-4

Stuttgart Open (2026) - Quarter-finals: Svitolina

The first meeting between these two occurred at the Aussie Open two years ago, when Svitolina was forced to retire with a severe back injury.

Later that year in Mexico, Noskova won 91% of her first serves, with two break points to take the win.

Svitolina earned her first win against Noskova in Germany this year, hitting 11 aces without a single double fault.

Svitolina has played a lot of tennis in a short time, and at her age, we do not believe she will have the energy to outlast Noskova this weekend.

#1683. Opinion: England international suggests Liverpool could soon have the best player in the world

Liverpool want to return to the pinnacle of football, and for that they need the best players on the planet.

Richard Hughes was very much motivated by this philosophy. It's why he spent so lavishly as the sporting director of the club.

He wanted to bring in the best players on the market. He did that. On paper he was successful. He secured Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz.

Not to mention other players for whom there was a lot of competition for as well. This includes Milos Kerkez, Jeremy Jacquet, Hugo Ekitike and Giorgi Mamardashvili.

Now aside from the notable exceptions like Ekitike and Jacquet, it's true that so far the aforementioned players have not lived up to their hype.

But transfers are judged in the long-term, not the short-term.

Julian Ward is overseeing a major reshuffleHughes has left behind a bit of a disjointed squad. Ward's job is now to fix that as Liverpool's new sporting director. It's not going to be easy. But the good thing is that the spine of the team is strong. You can comfortably build a team around Isak, Wirtz, Ekitike, Jacquet and Barcola. These are players who could become superstars and who absolutely have what it takes to be world-beaters. On top of that it's important to mention how smartly Liverpool recruited at youth level. Ifeanyi Ndukwe already looks like an incredible value for money. Mor Talla Ndiaye could prove to be the same. Let's not forget about Lucca Brughmanns and Samuel Martinez either who are very highly regarded in their respective age-groups.

On top of that it's important to mention how smartly Liverpool recruited at youth level. Ifeanyi Ndukwe already looks like an incredible value for money.

Mor Talla Ndiaye could prove to be the same. Let's not forget about Lucca Brughmanns and Samuel Martinez either who are very highly regarded in their respective age-groups.

Now on top of this, there's already an exciting academy thronging with burgeoning talent ready to break into Andoni Iraola's first-team.

This season's revelation has been Trey Nyoni, who has been absolutely sublime.

Rio Ngumoha has also been sensational. It's easy to forget that this is still only the beginning for the 18-year-old. Quansah who has now trained with him at club and international level speaking to BBC 5 Live confirmed that he believed that eventually Liverpool could have one of the best players on the planet.

“Rio Ngumoha," Quansah replied when asked on who he believes could win the Ballon d'Or.

"Outstanding, outstanding talent. Trained with him at Liverpool a lot," he continued.

“He’s so sharp, so quick. He’s so brave at doing his one-v-ones and definitely someone who has potential to be on that level.”

By the sounds of it, in Ngumoha Liverpool could soon be welcoming the best player on the planet.

#1682. Manager of the season is a one-horse race, Man United have taken incompetence to new levels and Newcastle to go down? Our experts' verdict on the Premier League so far

Published: 15:31 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:39 EST, 11 November 2026

With ten games of the Premier League season gone, it's time for another breather as the second international break rolls around. Here's our experts' verdict on the season so far...

Ronald Araujo. The Uruguayan on loan at Liverpool from Barcelona has gone some way to solving a huge problem for Andoni Iraola at right-back. IAN LADYMAN

Pascal Gross – epitome of the Brighton formula. The first signing when they reached the Premier League now back for his second spell. Supreme confidence in the model shines through him. He is understated and over delivering at 35. MATT BARLOW

Martin Odegaard. A sensational footballer. Few players can control those around them in the manner that the Arsenal skipper does, and he is scoring important goals, too. CRAIG HOPE

Brighton's Diego Gomez and Pascal Gross both receive nominations for player of the season so far from Daily Mail Sport's experts

Diego Gomez. You can’t argue with two goal of the season contenders already – one of them from the halfway line. Wonderful midfielder who is integral to how Brighton play. JACK GAUGHAN

Pascal Gross. The Brighton midfielder has covered more ground than any player in the league thus far and is third in the league for goal contributions with eight. A midfield conductor that has hit all the right notes (outside of that one lapse at Anfield with his own goal). NATHAN SALT

Pascal Gross. Three goals, four assists, and such creative and organisational influence from the 35-year-old. He gives Brighton control, finds ways through congested midfields and brings an authority to their pressing game, starting every game and playing more minutes than any team-mate. IAN HERBERT

Declan Rice – Toughie, this. I’ll plump for Rice for his sheer consistency at the heart of an Arsenal side at the top of the table. Mr Reliable. KIERAN GILL

Pascal Gross. Bloke is in his mid-30s, started every Brighton game, has scored four goals, set up another four, meaning only Erling Haaland and Evanilson (an honourable mention for this gong) have combined for more, and has created at least five more chances than any other player in the division. He’s at the heart of everything Brighton do. JAMES SHARPE

Rayan Cherki. Man City’s gifted No10 has been in outstanding form even if his team haven’t. Cherki’s cracking goal in Saturday’s defeat at Nottingham Forest was his seventh of the season on top of three assists. CHRIS WHEELER

Fabian Hurzeler. We are almost a third of the way through the season and Brighton are in second place. The odds are still hugely stacked against them but if they keep up their form, they will be the most unlikely title challengers since Leicester City. OLIVER HOLT

Fabian Hurzeler. We thought Chris Hughton did a good job at Brighton. Ditto Graham Potter and Roberto de Zerbi. But Hurzeler has taken the Seagulls to a different level and all that with the challenge of playing European football thrown in too. Hat tips here also for David Moyes, Keith Andrews, Marco Rose and Sergej Jakirovic. IAN LADYMAN

Fabian Hurzeler – has Brighton in with a genuine chance of a Champions League place as others falter and they continue to build despite selling important players (Baleba & Welbeck) and suffering injuries (Mitoma & Minteh). They play an exciting brand of attractive football, develop young individuals in a team and are handling European football. MATT BARLOW

Fabian Hurzeler. His Brighton team are the best to watch in the division and that is because they are well coached and exact a plan, which opponents are currently unable to combat. Champions League football awaits. CRAIG HOPE

It has to be Fabian Hurzeler. Beaten both Arsenal and Manchester City, hammered Aston Villa and smashed their rivals. Brighton are flying. JACK GAUGHAN

Fabian Hurzeler. Brighton are the Premier League's top scorers, have inflicted Arsenal's only defeat and the Seagulls are flying high as the closest challenger to the Gunners sat in 2nd in the November international break. Marco Rose gets an honourable mention for how well Bournemouth have fared post-Andoni Iraola. NATHAN SALT

Fabian Hurzeler has led Brighton to second place with seven wins from their first ten games

Fabian Hurzeler, Brighton. Yes, he’s working with the players produced by the Tony Bloom data algorithms but he’s adapting those players to games. He didn’t try to outplay Arsenal at their own game, instead making the match chaotic and physically demanding. IAN HERBERT

Fabian Hurzeler – To think a naff Christmas last season prompted claims from your usual In The Knows that Brighton were considering sacking Hurzeler. They stuck with him, and now he has his side sitting second in the Premier League. KIERAN GILL

Fabian Hurzeler. It’s got to be, hasn’t it? He has Brighton second in the Premier League, completely on merit, and fifth in the Conference League. They play beautiful football and are fully in the title race. Some people wanted him sacked last season. JAMES SHARPE

Fabian Hurzeler . Fantastic achievement to guide Brighton to second place in the Premier League a quarter of the way into the season, beating both Arsenal and Manchester City. They are also performing well in the UEFA Conference and won away at Manchester United in the Carabao Cup before going out of the competition to City on penalties. CHRIS WHEELER

Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Brighton. Arsenal are a smooth-running machine. They strengthened well in the summer and are already reaping the rewards. OLIVER HOLT

Arsenal, Man City, Liverpool, Chelsea, Man United. IAN LADYMAN

Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea, Brighton, Spurs. Assuming City are deducted points here I'm backing Liverpool to emerge as closest challengers, Brighton to stay the course and both Spurs and Chelsea to eventually feel the benefit of not being in Europe. MATT BARLOW

Arsenal. Brighton. Manchester City. Liverpool. Chelsea. That is the current order and, Bournemouth apart, I can't see any other team challenging for the top five. Brighton don't have to fall away, as some suggest. They are too well drilled for their position to simply be an upshot of a fast start or momentum. What they have feels more permanent. CRAIG HOPE

Arsenal, Manchester City*, Liverpool, Brighton, Chelsea. City’s second place is pending the fallout of their appeal and any sanctions handed down. Aston Villa and Tottenham will fancy taking a run at the top five but Chelsea and Liverpool should continue improving. Bournemouth are an outside bet too. JACK GAUGHAN

Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Brighton, Chelsea. NATHAN SALT

Arsenal, Liverpool, Brighton, Aston Villa, Chelsea. IAN HERBERT

Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea, Man City, Brighton. Arsenal will win the Premier League, obviously. Manchester City will be distracted by all the chaos. Brighton will sneak a top-five finish with help from their fine start. KIERAN GILL

Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City, Chelsea, Brighton. CHRIS WHEELER

Newcastle United, Coventry City, Ipswich Town. I still think that Newcastle will get sucked into trouble. And I think that the inexperience of their manager will cost them when things get tight. OLIVER HOLT

Man City (deducted points), Crystal Palace, Coventry. Again, a massive guess involved re the City penalty but it's always guesswork even when educated. Isn't it? Fear Coventry will fade and Palace have simply lost too many good players for a managerial change to save them. MATT BARLOW

Hull. Coventry. Crystal Palace. Hull just cannot win enough games and that will catch up with them. Coventry don't have the quality over the course of a season, while Palace look like a side who have lost belief in themselves, their manager and the direction of the club. CRAIG HOPE

Coventry, Ipswich Town, Hull City. While all have enjoyed varying degrees of encouraging starts, the teams around them are either set to change managers or emerging from sluggish form. JACK GAUGHAN

Coventry's defeat at Everton on Friday leaves them one place above the drop zone - and all of our writers are predicting them to go down

Ipswich Town, Coventry City, Crystal Palace. NATHAN SALT

Coventry, Crystal Palace, Sunderland. IAN HERBERT

Crystal Palace, Ipswich, Coventry. Of the three newly-promoted clubs, I’m saying Hull will stay in the Premier League, and Crystal Palace, even with a new manager, will continue to struggle. KIERAN GILL

Coventry, Sunderland, Palace. This is the season Palace go. Only Thomas Frank can save them now. JAMES SHARPE

Daniel Farke. He's been around a long time to be a surprise package but after years of people saying he wasn't good enough to keep a team in the Premier League, his Leeds team is not just surviving but excelling. OLIVER HOLT

I have loved watching Oli McBurnie play for Hull. He leads the line, he sets the tone and he scores the odd goal. A throwback centre-forward. IAN LADYMAN

Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic... given the Tigers a platform they can build on and avoid being drawn into a relegation battle. MATT BARLOW

Bournemouth, their manager Marco Rose and striker Evanilson. I saw them play earlier in the season during a six-match winless league start and, despite that, you knew they would come good. Like Brighton, they look well coached under Rose and, in Evanilson, they have a striker who has now scored in five straight league games. They could yet gatecrash the top five. CRAIG HOPE

James McAtee is beginning to show a real run of consistent form in Nottingham Forest’s midfield and if he continues with that, might well be knocking on Thomas Tuchel’s door come March. JACK GAUGHAN

Evanilson (right) has been a revelation for Bournemouth and Marco Rose

Hull City. Widely panned as being the side that would break Derby County's points record en route to an immediate relegation back to the Championship but they've more than held their own so far. Going unbeaten at home to this point is a good sign for survival hopes. NATHAN SALT

Everton. The dismal and chaotic summer window under Friedkin Group, who now want out, left you thinking that it would be another season of struggle but David Moyes remains the most under-celebrated manager in the division. He’s even getting goals out of Thierno Barry. Sixth spot, two shy of Liverpool, is extraordinary. IAN HERBERT

Everton. When their £40million move for Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave them with only one striker, I thought they were done for. Underestimate David Moyes at your peril, I guess, because they’re now sixth in the Premier League. Kudos. KIERAN GILL

Nicolas Jackson. Found his home immediately at Villa, with nine goals already this season, and proving that Chelsea were too hasty to write him off. Looks so sharp in front of goal and a focal point Unai Emery can build his team around. JAMES SHARPE

Charalampos Kostoulas – the Greek teenager was mainly used off the bench last season, but has seized his chance following Danny Welbeck’s move to Chelsea with five goals and four assists in all competitions. CHRIS WHEELER

Enzo Fernandez. Manchester City fans are starting to realise why some Chelsea supporters were glad to see the back of him, both on the field and off it. OLIVER HOLT

Manchester United. I didn’t expect them to be quite this bad. Michael Carrick and his team have taken incompetence to new levels. IAN LADYMAN

Take your pick at Old Trafford. Michael Carrick? Bruno Fernandes? Lisandro Martinez? His pal Jason Wilcox? Sir Jim & the Glazers? Maybe the roofers? Probably a good time for collective responsibility, an award for Man United. MATT BARLOW

Manchester United. Why complicate it? Even with a change of manager, which is necessary, there is close to no chance they'll recover to qualify again for the Champions League, and for a club of Man United's size there can be no greater underachievement. CRAIG HOPE

Even by their standards, Manchester United’s first three months – in the relegation zone after a round of matches for the first time in 40 years – has been beyond dismal. JACK GAUGHAN

Manchester United. They are absolutely shocking from the boardroom to the pitch. You've got unqualified and indecisive executives calling the shots and a bunch of players who need to wake up and realise they are in a relegation battle. Diogo Dalot almost took this award but United's problems are bigger than his own ineptitude. NATHAN SALT

Manchester United's chances of returning to the Champions League already look over

Manchester United. Yes, they have been serially failed by owners and have incapable defenders but that league position is beyond all belief. Even this weekend, Bryan Mbeumo and Mason Mount have looked shadows of the players United signed. IAN HERBERT

Bruno Fernandes. Fabulous footballer, obviously, but he has been substandard in what he is providing on the pitch, both as a creator and in his approach to leadership and that is not helping Manchester United right now. KIERAN GILL

Newcastle. Yes, losing Eddie Howe was always going to take some getting used to and, yes, when you look down their team sheet you wonder where all the quality has gone but they shouldn’t be this bad. Opta has them bottom of their expected points table. JAMES SHARPE

Man Utd – from the boardroom to the dressing-room, they are in a mess. Expect United to find some degree of form and move up the table, but this season already feels like a write-off. CHRIS WHEELER

Manchester United. They blew all the momentum Michael Carrick built last season with a desperate summer transfer window. They need to try to remedy that in January. OLIVER HOLT

Tottenham. They need a centre-forward. The rest of the team is starting to look as though it has some balance. IAN LADYMAN

Richarlison's PR team, and Man United still so desperately short of the quality they need in so many key areas. MATT BARLOW

Newcastle. If they are to persist with a new formation of 4-2-3-1 which incorporates a No10 under Matthias Jaissle, they have to go out and sign a No10 rather than playing strikers or midfielders there. There is a danger they could be dragged into the bottom three before Christmas. CRAIG HOPE

Jacob Murphy thought he had secured a win for Newcastle at Fulham on Saturday but they ended with a 1-1 draw and now sit 12th, four points above the drop

Crystal Palace’s outgoing coach Pierre Sage has already mentioned the winter transfer window and they have holes to plug in that squad if they are to survive. JACK GAUGHAN

Sunderland. Injuries have started to pile up – they are up to nine right now – and they desperately need to freshen things up as they juggle European football and a relegation battle. They have good players but need to ruffle a few feathers with arrivals to improve results. NATHAN SALT

Manchester United. If Sir Jim Ratcliffe doesn’t know by now that a striker and functioning left back are direly needed, then he is even dimmer than we imagined him to be. The problem is that United, having thrown millions after players in the past decade or so, do not have much more. IAN HERBERT

Crystal Palace. Not only do they need a new manager, they have to help him by bringing in new bodies in January. Pierre Sage has even said so: ‘We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions.’ KIERAN GILL

Crystal Palace. They needed to do it in the summer and didn’t but the opening ten games of the season have made it abundantly clear that Palace have to replace Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix properly. Otherwise they are down. JAMES SHARPE

United still need the striker and left-back they should have signed in the summer to cover for Benjamin Sesko and Luke Shaw. It was an act of negligence not to do so. CHRIS WHEELER

Manchester City to be hit with a points deduction that takes them out of the running for any position in the top five. And probably more. OLIVER HOLT

Manchester United will get a shift on up the league table – if and when they appoint a good manager. IAN LADYMAN

If Brighton qualifying for the Champions League for the first time isn't big enough... maybe Leeds can qualify for Europe. MATT BARLOW

Odegaard will be footballer of the year and Eddie Howe will lead Man United into the top half of the Premier League (and probably Europa League qualification). CRAIG HOPE

Martin Odegaard is Craig Hope's pick to be named footballer of the year

There could be fewer than five managerial changes through the season – bucking the trend of the last few years. Sage and Michael Carrick both look precarious but others down there seem more settled in their jobs. JACK GAUGHAN

Alexander Isak will dethrone Erling Haaland to win the Golden Boot as Liverpool go closest to Arsenal in the title race. Too much was made of his difficulties last season when injuries were so disrupting. The service he will get from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha, Victor Munoz, Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola will keep him well fed. NATHAN SALT

Manchester City are not included in these final table predictions because they ought to be relegated from the division for serial and institutional cheating and don't justify incorporation. But I suspect they will find a way of suspending the justice which ought to come their way. Somehow, I just don’t see them being relegated in the way they should. They're happy to extend this interminable legal process. IAN HERBERT

Manchester United, somehow, finish in the top half. KIERAN GILL

Nottingham Forest will push for Europe. That victory over Manchester City had been coming. They were in the bottom three before the weekend but so much of that has been down to them failing to take any of the many chances they create. If Liam Delap can get firing like this, they will make a charge up this very average Premier League table. JAMES SHARPE

Sometime between now and May, a semblance of normality will return to Manchester United and fans will be looking back on these weeks when their club was in the relegation zone like it was a bad dream. CHRIS WHEELER

#1681. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool will be in pot one, while Manchester United and Aston Villa will be in pot two.

This evening’s ceremony should be getting underway in Monaco in a couple of minutes.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Gabriel misses his penalty ❌PSG WIN THE UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE!!! 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/6XSuU3xqsN

Cristiano Ronaldo 🖐️#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/WzeWLfEomZ

Mattéo Guendouzi, the former Arsenal fireband, was at the heart of chaotic and ugly scenes in the Champions League qualifying play-off between Lyon and his side Fenerbahce, culminating in a brawl at the mouth of the tunnel.

Guendouzi provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch in the aftermath of a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium that sent the Turkish outfit through to the Champions League group stage.

Matteo Guendouzi has not forgotten who his rivals are... 👀The former Marseille player made his feelings known as Fenerbahce knocked out Marseille's rivals Lyon. pic.twitter.com/pjDKPqPzZD

As he gestured towards the fans, while being shepherded by team-mates, objects were thrown from the crowd. A figure in what appears to be a Lyon tracksuit then emerged from the tunnel and seemed to try to aim a flying kick at Guendouzi.

Of the 36 teams in the draw, 29 qualified at the end of last season, while the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.

AEK, LASK, Viking, Slovan Bratislava, Sabah Baku, Fenerbahce and Bodo/Glimt were the seven teams to come through the play-offs.

For en kveld vi hadde på Aspmyra i går 😍 Høydepunktene fra kampen finner du nå i Glimt-appen pic.twitter.com/UPJQQgGmH9

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the Champions League draw in Monaco, with the 36 teams in this season’s competition finding out their eight league phase fixtures.

The teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal will be among the teams joining the Parisians in pot one, while the two remaining English teams, Manchester United and Aston Villa, will be in pot two.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

The draw is expected to get underway at 5pm.

#1680. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino's first signing 'completed' as major overhaul of Red Devils targeted

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 02:30

Manchester United have signed teenager Tyler Adjei from Reading and registered the centre-forward this week, the latest report has revealed.

The Red Devils confirmed the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as the replacement for Michael Carrick this week, and fans are keen for further changes at Old Trafford.

United are 18th in the Premier League, and many of the players in their squad have failed to prove that they are good enough to play for the club.

The January transfer window will be key for Pochettino, and it would not be surprising to see the team target younger stars in the coming months.

Teenager Adjei has become the first signing of the Pochettino era, according to The Athletic, with the 16-year-old having signed from Reading, and he is expected to head straight into Darren Fletcher's Under-18s side.

The signing of Adjei will not benefit Pochettino this season, but his addition will still be important for the future of the club given there are a number of stars that will need to be phased out.

Though captain Bruno Fernandes is the side's best attacker, he is 32 and has started to show signs of decline, and the Red Devils will need a successor to fill his void sooner rather than later.

Ensuring there is a steady stream of younger stars at the club will make replacing important first-team players much easier, especially as prices across Europe have become significantly inflated.

Fernandes is not the only ageing star at Old Trafford, with nine members of the team set to be 29 or older by the time the season ends.

Defenders Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are 33 and 31 respectively, while Lisandro Martinez and Diogo Dalot have frequently been linked with exits.

While the Red Devils need reinforcements in almost every area of the pitch, their most pressing needs are in the backline.

Younger talents would help secure the future of United's defence, though bringing in defenders in their twenties would also be beneficial to Pochettino in 2027.

#1679. Opinion: Arne Slot axed Liverpool star who is perfect for Andoni Iraola

Arne Slot's time as Liverpool's manager was fairly mixed.

He won the Premier League title during his first season in charge but then, just a year later, he was relieved of his duties.

Most fans wanted his sacking to occur months earlier but, Fenway Sports Group chose to stick by him and, luckily, he managed to get his men to qualify for the Champions League.

His fifth-place finish was clearly miles away from where Liverpool actually needed to be which is why Andoni Iraola was brought in.

And, while a lot of people thought his time at Anfield would be smooth-sailing, there are still a lot of changes he needs to make before his team are properly ready to compete for silverware again.

The main issues that need to be rectified are the performances of some players with the January transfer window the best way for them to fix the issues that they're suffering with.

But, while Slot was in charge, he had the answer to one of Iraola's main problems but, instead of keeping him around, he chose to move him on with fans now wondering why that decision was ever made.

Liverpool must figure out what they're doing with their midfield

Liverpool's main problem area among their first-team squad at the moment is their midfield.

They currently have four options to choose from as their number sixes and, while Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have put in some solid performances, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have both failed to do the same.

The duo were the two midfielders offered long-term contracts by FSG last season with each of them being handed bumper new deals.

Clearly, Liverpool expected them to be their regular midfield duo but, that has been far from the case.

Mac Allister and Nyoni have both performed far better than their teammates and, it feels like they should have been the ones given new contracts instead.

However, that isn't what happened and now, Iraola and Julian Ward seem to be stuck between a rock and a hard place.

So many positions within Liverpool's squad still need upgrading but, if Slot and Richard Hughes had kept one player they sold in the 2025-26 summer window, they'd have one less position to worry about.

Tyler Morton would have been perfect for Andoni Iraola

As mentioned, Liverpool's clear-out last season was taken differently depending on who you asked.

Some people believed that selling players such as Luis Diaz, Tyler Morton and Jarell Quansah was the best thing to do.

But, looking back now, all three of them had incredible campaigns last season and each of them would have been a huge help to Slot.

And, of the lot, Morton is probably the one that Liverpool wish they didn't let go, especially since he's the perfect defensive midfielder for Iraola's system.

Not only can he win duels, keep his line and add extra stability to a team but, he can also create chances and score them if needed.

Alongside all this, he's also a really hard-working central midfielder so, the fact that each of these skills line up perfectly with Iraola's system is a real kick in the teeth.

Obviously, what's done is done and these things can't be changed now but, in hindsight, selling a Liverpool-born midfielder who wanted nothing else but to play for his childhood club was maybe not the Reds' best idea.

That is, especially when they already knew that their midfield was going to be a problem for them.
